parsed.rationale: Both `PlayerState.isActive` (line 72 in PlayerState.swift) and `PlaybackState.isActive` (line 96 in PlaybackState.swift) are computed properties in the same `Playback` package with a Jaccard similarity of 0.71, indicating near-identical implementations. Since both types live in the same package (`Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore`) and neither is test, codegen, mock, or sample-app code, the duplication is unintentional. The idiomatic Swift resolution is to introduce a shared protocol (e.g., `ActiveStateProviding`) with a default `isActive` implementation in a protocol extension, allowing both `PlayerState` and `PlaybackState` to conform and delete their individual implementations. This centralises the logic and makes the shared semantic ('is this state active?') explicit in the type system.
